Subject: Pilot ops catalogue & cost scenarios

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for taking this—NimboAI is preparing a 3-month pilot to validate generation latency and per-token economics for our multi-turn chat feature (typical seq length ~1024, peak concurrency ~120 rps). We want a simple catalogue of options and ballpark costing so we can take to our finance and infra leads. Specifically: 

- A “cache-first” pilot focused on KV/prefix caching (expect many repeated prefixes) and minimal quantization.
- A “quant-first” pilot with aggressive int8/int4 recommendations and expected accuracy delta.
- A hybrid path that balances latency and unit cost.

Could you provide: a short ops catalogue with recommended config for each path, estimated per-token cost and expected 95th pct latency, and any recommended model/quant combo? Also please flag any capabilities (e.g., private deployment or dedicated pools) that materially change cost.

Can we get a draft by EOD tomorrow? If easier, we can do a 30-min sync—I'm available tomorrow 13:00–16:00 PT.

Thanks,
Anna
Head of Product, NimboAI

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-02T10:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Pilot ops catalogue & cost scenarios

Hi Anna — appreciate the context. Attached is a compact ops catalogue and a draft pricing play that maps the three approaches to concrete settings and cost bands. High-level summary inline: 

1) Cache-first pilot (recommended if >35% prefix reuse):
   - Runtime: hosted with dedicated pool (burstable), KV caching enabled, minimal quantization (fp16).
   - Expected 95th pct latency: 180–260ms at 120 rps.
   - Estimated token unit cost: $0.0018–$0.0025 (depends on cache hit-rate).

2) Quant-first pilot (recommended if you need lowest $/token and accept small quality risk):
   - Runtime: dedicated pool; quantization to int8 (or int4 for non-critical outputs).
   - Expected 95th pct latency: 220–320ms.
   - Estimated token unit cost: $0.0011–$0.0016.
   - Note: quality regression varies by prompt; we include baseline eval for your prompt set.

3) Hybrid (balanced):
   - KV + prefix caching + int8 quantization on model weights.
   - Expected 95th pct latency: 170–280ms.
   - Estimated token unit cost: $0.0013–$0.0019.

Attachments: ops_catalogue_v1.pdf (catalogue), pilot-pricing-draft.pdf (commercials). Jordan's attached spreadsheet has the quantization expectations for a couple of model families.

Proposed next steps:
- I can prep a one-page slide with the recommended pilot path you prefer (cache-first or hybrid) and a sample SOW/credit proposal.
- If you want the draft by EOD tomorrow, let's lock a sync at 14:00 PT tomorrow—works on my end.

Best,
Hannah
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2027-04-02T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Pilot ops catalogue & cost scenarios

Quick technical note (see attached quantization_matrix.xlsx):

- For multi-turn chat with seq=1024, our empirical results show int8 + KV caching keeps generation quality within ~1.5–3% of fp16 on open weights for common LLM families. Latency impact is modest; throughput improves ~20–40% depending on kernel choices.
- If you have hallucination-sensitive outputs, consider keeping the last n layers fp16 (mixed precision) and quantizing the rest — this often preserves factuality while giving cost wins.
- We recommend running a short quality eval on ~500 representative prompts to validate the delta; we can run that as part of the pilot (included).

Jordan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
